html:
José Ramos-Horta spent the years of Indonesian occupation abroad as the spokesman of the Timorese resistance. He shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1996 with Bishop Carlos Belo.

A founder of Fretilin, he left Timor just before the invasion of 1975 and spent 24 years lobbying the United Nations and foreign governments, where few listened until the Santa Cruz massacre.

After independence he became foreign minister, prime minister and president. He was badly wounded in an assassination attempt in 2008, recovered, and was elected president again in 2022. He has worked closely with Xanana Gusmão.
